reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to take any real number—ranging from negative infinity to positive infinity—and map it into a clean, bounded range between zero and one. A linear function fails here because it grows without bound. Instead, we use the logistic sigmoid function. By placing an exponential term in the denominator, the function gracefully saturates at zero for large negative inputs and at one for large positive inputs.

As we adjust the steepness parameter $k$, the transition becomes sharper or more gradual. Changing the midpoint $x_0$ shifts the entire S-shaped curve horizontally. At any given point on the curve, the derivative tells us the local rate of change, showing that the steepest growth always happens right at the midpoint.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any real number into the range $0$ to $1$. Adjust the steepness and midpoint to see how the S-shaped curve stretches and shifts.
